title: Ansel and the Scholarship
premise: Hazel Pemberton has been holding her family together on caffeine and denial since her father left, so when a group chat called 'The Scholarship' starts texting her predictions that come true, she assumes it's a cruel prank. But the chat is run by three students who discovered the school board buried a scholarship fund — money meant for kids like Hazel — and they need someone with nothing left to lose to help expose it. As the predictions escalate from uncanny to dangerous, Hazel must choose between protecting her siblings' fragile stability and telling a truth that could burn down the only institution keeping them afloat. In the end, Hazel testifies at a packed school board meeting before prom, the fund is restored, and she learns that survival isn't the same as silence.
about_author: Coral Montrose is the pen name of a former night-shift nurse who wrote her first novel in the break room between rounds. She writes stories about kids who grow up too fast and the small rebellions that give them their childhoods back.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A chaotic morning establishes Hazel's world: burnt toast, missing permission slips, mom's night-shift exhaustion, and Hazel's iron rule that no one outside the family learns how thin things are. When a text arrives from an unknown number predicting tomorrow's fire drill to the minute, she deletes it. Emotional beat: weary control masking quiet dread.

chapters.title: The Group Chat
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with interludes of the chat itself. The predictions keep coming true — a pop quiz, a pipe burst, her brother Milo's scraped knee — until the chat invites her by name: 'We know about the Pemberton Fund.' She researches and finds a 1998 endowment that vanished from district records. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: Three Strangers and a Secret
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Hazel meets the chat's authors — Priya, Dev, and quiet transfer student Marcus — in the library basement. They've traced the fund through decades of board minutes; every year it was 'deferred' while administrators' pet projects grew. They want Hazel because her family was named in the original bequest. Emotional beat: wary alliance over shared anger.

chapters.title: What Survival Costs
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Mom picks up extra shifts to cover a school fee the fund should have paid, and Hazel covers the house alone — cooking, homework patrol, lying to a social worker who knocks. The chapter shows exactly what exposing the board could cost: stability, Mom's job, custody scrutiny. Emotional beat: the price of truth made concrete.

chapters.title: Predictions
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The group tests whether the chat predicts or causes events when a forecast — 'the auditor visits Friday' — comes true, suggesting someone inside the district is feeding them information. Dev gets followed home. The four realize the board knows what they're digging into. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening like a fist.

chapters.title: Prom Is a Weapon
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The board schedules its rubber-stamp vote on 'discretionary reallocation' for prom week, betting no one will notice. The group plans to crash the meeting with evidence, but Hazel balks — her name on the complaint means her family under a microscope. First fracture in the alliance. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth turns personal.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Someone leaks Hazel's family's financial records to the school, and Mom is summoned to a 'support meeting' that feels like a threat. Hazel realizes the board will use her siblings against her. She nearly quits — then Milo asks why rich kids get everything, and she can't lie to him. Emotional beat: rock bottom, and the choice made anyway.

chapters.title: Buried
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Racing the vote, the group breaks into the district annex and finds the original bequest file — including proof a former board member diverted funds to a private account, still on the current board. They photograph everything, but Marcus is caught on camera and detained. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Meeting Before Prom
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, climax. At the emergency board session, Marcus's detention galvanizes students and parents to pack the room. Hazel testifies — voice shaking, siblings in the front row — laying out the fund's history and the diversion. The whistleblower inside the district finally steps forward to corroborate. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into power.

chapters.title: The Pemberton Fund
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, resolution. The board member resigns under investigation; the fund is restored and renamed for the original donor's intent. Prom happens — Hazel goes, briefly, and leaves early not from duty but because she wants to. Home, she tells Milo the whole story, no more lies. Emotional beat: survival redefined as living, not just enduring.
